the calcium accumulation in HEPB-affected dentin is not a consequence of inhibition of mineralization but rather an intrinsic property of the non-mineralizing dentin matrix.
DPP may be responsible for calcium deposition in the circumpulpal matrix, whereas DSP and OPN may be involved in the mineralization of the mantle dentin.

the calcium accumulation observed in the circumpulpal region of dentin in the bisphosphonates-treated rats is not caused by the accumulation of any of the proteins examined in this study, including DSP, OPN, DPP and proteoglycan, and the mechanism of calcium accumulation in circupulpal dentin remains to be determined.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
DPP is the major calcium binding molecule in circumpulp dentin matrix.

the non-mineralization of circumpulp dentin matrix in HEBP-treated rats is not caused by a defect in mineralization of the collagen matrix, but rather by a defect in the accumulation of calcium in the circumpulpal non-collagen matrix, possibly DPP.
DPP is the most likely molecule responsible for calcium accumulation and mineralization of circumpulpally located dentin matrix.
